scenes.line1: Why do APIs care about HTTP versions?
scenes.line2: And what do those methods mean?
scenes.say: Ever wondered why APIs care about HTTP versions, or what those GET and POST methods really mean?

scenes.label: Methods
scenes.sub: GET fetches data, POST submits, PUT replaces, DELETE removes.
scenes.say: HTTP methods signal your intent. GET fetches data, POST submits new info, PUT replaces a resource, and DELETE removes it.
HTTP one point one sends text and handles one request at a time. HTTP two brings multiplexing and header compression. HTTP three runs over QUIC for even faster connections.

scenes.question: What's PUT usually used for?
scenes.right: PUT is for replacing a resource, not partial updates. PATCH is for partial changes.
scenes.say: Here's a classic interview trap. PUT is for replacing a resource, not partial updates. PATCH handles partial changes.
